name: Ketuanan Melayu
summary: Ketuanan Melayu (Malay supremacy) holds that the Malays, as the native people and heirs of the Malay rulers, are entitled to political primacy in Malaysia. Its advocates treat the 1957 constitution as a social contract in which non-Malays received citizenship and Malays received the special position, Malay as national language, Islam as the Federation's religion and the sovereignty of the rulers. In practice it has meant ethnic preferences in education, public employment and business under the New Economic Policy.
scope: The Malaysian doctrine as stated by its advocates (Abdullah Ahmad's 1986 formulation as reported by Marzali, and Marzali's own defence) and as written into the Federal Constitution (Articles 3, 32, 89, 152, 153, 160), together with the record of UMNO-led governments since 1970 as described by Tayeb. It excludes Malay nationalism in general, Islamist movements, and critics' accounts. The evidence base is narrow, so most statements are null.

furtherReading.title: Isu Ketuanan Melayu di Malaysia (Amri Marzali, 2021)
furtherReading.note: A scholarly defence of the doctrine, with an English abstract.

furtherReading.title: Federal Constitution of Malaysia (Constitute)
furtherReading.note: The text of Articles 3, 152, 153 and 160 on which the doctrine rests.
